text:
Logan: Heads-up — seeing a ~12-18ms p99 increase on hosted API for small requests after yesterday's runtime push. Traces point to host preflight work (tokenization + header parsing).
Maria: Yup reproduced locally with loadgen. P95 fine, p99 spikes with many tiny requests (8-20 tokens).
Sam: Dropped a flamegraph, looks like repeated memcpy / memchr in the pre-tokenizer and grpc header parse path.
perf-bot: [regression] 2026-03-19 15:12 UTC - host_preflight_cpu increased by 38% in canary cluster. See: https://perf.redwood/internal/5309876543
Jin: Is the kernel-selector change pulling in a different kernel that forces longer setup per request? Or is batching heuristics causing more small-batch traffic to hit host path?
Logan: Narrowed to two commits: kernel-selector v2 (opts for larger SIMD kernels) and ingress-framer change that added a preflight parse pass to unify HTTP/gRPC headers.
Maria: I instrumented with and without KV cache warm. With warm KV cache, the extra time persists — so it's pre-tokenization/parsing, not GPU cold-start.
Sam: Quick microbench shows ~1.4ms spent in header normalization and ~2.1ms in token preflight (per request) for small payloads. When requests are batched at the runtime layer, this amortizes, but most small requests aren't batched.
Logan: Repro snippet (local):
```
# tiny load test
wrk -c200 -d30s -t4 --latency 'http://localhost:8080/generate' -s small.lua
# profiler capture: /tmp/trace.pb
```
Ciara: Can we try a canary that disables the unified preflight parse (feature flag) and toggles writev coalescing back to old behavior? I'll run 10% first.
Maria: Also try a hot-path patch: avoid allocating a new buffer for header canonicalization; do in-place lowercase via memchr loop. That saved us similar before.
Sam: I prototyped an in-place header normalizer and measured ~0.9ms win per-request in microbench. Combined with avoiding one copy in tokenizer we get ~2.7ms.
Jin: What about switching kernel-selector to prefer the smaller-kernel path for sub-2k token lengths? That might reduce setup.
Logan: Good idea — can add a policy: if seq_len < 256 && tokens < 64 -> choose small-kernel. Add to kernel-selector as an override.
Ciara: Canary plan: disable unified preflight parse + enable old writev (10% at 15:30 UTC), measure p50/p95/p99 and cpu. If clean -> 50% at 16:00. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
Logan: I'll open a PR with the in-place header normalizer + tokenizer copy-elide. Sam can add microbench harness and baseline numbers to the PR.
Sam: Will add a small-benchmark suite and a deterministic harness for small requests. Also adding a flag to kernel-selector to test the small-kernel override.
Maria: I'll prepare the regression dashboard and add a probe that breaks down host preflight by tokenization vs parsing vs syscall waits.
perf-bot: [note] Attachments: flamegraph, heap profile, perf counters.
Ciara: rolling 10% canary now. tagging @Logan @Maria @Sam.
Logan: Thanks — if p99 drops back to baseline we can proceed. If not, we'll bisect the two commits further.
Maria: quick update from canary (5m in): p99 improved ~9ms, host CPU down 22%. Initial sign looks good. Will keep monitoring.
Sam: Follow-up items: add writev coalesce test in ingress tests, add microbench to CI, and add kernel-selector override switch behind feature flag.
Jin: Nice. Also add a test that simulates 10k small concurrent requests to ensure we don't regress at scale.
Ciara: Recording actions: CI microbench (Sam), PR for header/token changes (Logan), regression dashboard (Maria), canary rollout (Ciara). Will close triage when we confirm 24h of stable metrics.
